title: Creating with freedom to stop

captions.emotions: Enjoying the fruits of your work

meaning: A strong shared desire can produce tangible results while involvement leaves you free to choose whether to continue.
text: A shared undertaking can become so absorbing that stopping starts to feel like a loss. The Devil in the physical position of Manipura describes actions tied to immediate reward: repeating a successful move, obtaining more and securing a pleasant feeling. The Devil in energy identifies the motive, holding onto that promised enjoyment, sometimes at the expense of choosing another step. The Empress in emotions allows fullness and delight in the fruits you receive. The repeated Devil distinguishes a binding pattern of action from the pull sustaining it. A pleasing result does not remove the possibility of confinement.

For example, you make candles for a shared corner at home. Several look lovely already, but trying every mould and fragrance immediately feels tempting. **A result brings freer enjoyment when continuing can be chosen afresh.** Finished candles offer tangible pleasure even if some materials wait until another occasion. The undertaking need not fill the evening for you to consider it worthwhile.

The difficulty starts if new results become necessary to confirm the connection itself. You continue because stopping seems to mean abandoning shared desire. The abundance grows while opportunities to appreciate it shrink. Different wishes invite pressure for another batch or a little more time. Feeling satisfied can be sufficient reason to finish, preserving participation that need not constantly prove itself through another result.
